rows.note: This is the all-purpose everyday way to say a smaller amount or number, as in 少啲錢 or 少啲人.

example.english: Please put less sugar in this coffee.
example.jyutping: ni1 bui1 gaa3 fe1 siu2 di1 tong4 m4 goi1

rows.note: Use this when stressing that the amount or number is not as large as a comparison point, as in 冇咁多人.

example.english: There are less people today, so walking around is much more comfortable.
example.traditional: 今日冇咁多人，行街舒服好多。
example.jyutping: gam1 jat6 mou5 gam3 do1 jan4 haang4 gaai1 syu1 fuk6 hou2 do1

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for saying that something has a lesser degree or intensity.

example.jyutping: ni1 go3 fong1 faat3 mou5 gam3 jau5 haau6

rows.note: Use this when less refers to an amount, frequency, or quantity, especially after a verb such as 食少啲.

example.jyutping: nei5 jam2 siu2 di1 zau2 laa1

rows.note: Use this for the softened negative sense ‘not very ADJ’, as in something being less than helpful.

example.english: His explanation is less than helpful.
example.jyutping: keoi5 go3 gong2 faat3 m4 hai6 gei2 jau5 jung6

rows.traditional: A 冇 B 咁 + ADJ
rows.note: Use this explicit comparison when A is less ADJ than B.

example.english: Today is less cold than yesterday.
example.jyutping: gam1 jat6 mou5 kam4 jat6 gam3 dung3
